name: Electric tweezers
lead: Electric tweezers is a name used for two different things: powered tweezers (a motor-driven gripping tool, covered by patents such as a 2006 filing for a motorised tweezer) and, in hair removal, tweezers that pass an electrical signal through the tip to damage the hair root so it does not regrow.[1][2] Wikipedia describes the latter as an intended method of depilation.[1]
The term also appears in physics, where "electric tweezers" use electric fields to manipulate nanoparticles, which is unrelated to appearance.[3]
No clinical studies of electric tweezers for hair removal were found.
infobox: Electrical signal at tweezer tip to damage hair root

paras: Ordinary tweezers have been used for plucking hair since antiquity, with metal examples from Mesopotamia and India around 3000 BC.[1] Electric versions add a signal at the tip intended to prevent regrowth; the Wikipedia article gives no safety or efficacy data.[1]
Published work titled "electric tweezers" concerns nanoparticle manipulation, not cosmetic devices.[3]

card.summary: Battery-powered pluckers, some sold with a claim of damaging the root; no human studies found.
card.note: Efficacy and safety claims for the electrified type are untested in the sources found.

quick.overview:
Electric tweezers are powered tweezers sold for plucking hair; some are described as sending an electrical signal to the root.

No clinical evidence was found.
quick.mechanism: Motorised grip, or an electrical signal at the tip intended to damage the root.
quick.risks: No safety data were found; skin irritation is a general plucking risk.
